blockers: The main branch has NO protection at all - gh api repos/:owner/:repo/branches/main/protection returns 404, Branch not protected. No required PR, no required status checks, so a raw push to main bypasses clean-room-verify and Test & Quality. This is GitHub configuration only the operator can apply, and it should be applied BEFORE the promotion PR merges, not after.

The gate reports SAFE, a clean fast-forward with main +0 commits / +0 files, and would-publish 0. Clean-room Verify does NOT run on a push to develop; it is the PR gate, which is why the PR is the rite and not a formality.
Finish the seven remaining lane entries, cheapest first, each shrinking the ratchet in its own commit. The lane doc records the order and the honest price of each.

Make the before-push lane's declared scope true. It declares validationScope branchRange but runs tidy-imports against the DIRTY TREE, so with several agents sharing one checkout the gate goes red for files that are not even in the push. Measured, not fixed: agentFinishSteps is a static array and making it per-lane changes the JSON handoff contract, so it needs the handoffs lane. Half an afternoon, not twenty minutes.

The credential scope, verb to verb x object, still before spec slices 6-8. Scope is a closed enum of three variants with almost nothing issued against it, so widening now is a toy migration and widening later is a v2 plus a coexistence window.

GitHub Copilot as a real provider and the fourth budget axis it will demand - requests per billing period, a quota that REFILLS, which none of the three axes model. Missing: a Rust route and a GitHub OAuth device flow. BudgetDeclaration's fields are all optional, so the fourth axis is additive when the pressure is real.
open_questions: THE HATCH - how refarm is born on a device, and what the current workspace means. Agreed to become its own spec. What the measurement already establishes: workspaces are a FLAT map today (id -> path, kind); workspaceNamespaces is NOT sub-workspaces; and self-declaration already exists, since this repo declares refarm -> path dot in its own config. VERIFIED LIVE 2026-08-04 on this node: refarm workspace list returns two declared workspaces (rcdc5 at ~/git/rcdc5/rcdc5, refarm at dot), refarm workspace status returns 2 ok / 0 failed with the turbo executor detected and the local cache ready, and rcdc5 carries a shell-free named-command allowlist whose vpn entry connects the Serpro VPN. So the organic model is not a proposal - it is running. A declaration can live in TWO places and the pair describes an adoption path: a project that carries no refarm config gets declared IN THE NODE config so it can be operated at all (rcdc5 today), and a project that has adopted refarm carries its own. The node declaration is the BOOTSTRAP, not a degenerate case. Second half, from the operator: the node's own workspace should be VERSIONED, because recreating this node elsewhere today means re-writing by hand its workspace, delivery, surface, process and budget declarations.

Where does the workspace identity come from, per surface? refarm dispatch now HAS a --workspace flag binding a dispatch to a declared workspace id, so the CLI surface is answered and D9's workspace level is reachable from it. Still open for every other surface: a declared operation carries its workspace implicitly, refarm ask and chat cannot declare a budget at all, and no effort builder outside dispatch sets workspaceId.

Should the observation record which axes were ENFORCED, not just which were declared? max_usd.enforced exists because a currency ceiling cannot bind outside api pricing mode. The same question applies to the other two: on the event-dispatch path no axis binds at all, and within the respond path three sub-cases still record a full budget family with no watcher having run.

How does the CLI learn the CURRENT rate table? It derives it from the newest observation's own stamp, which detects relative staleness among observed runs but cannot see the cold-start case: bump RATE_TABLE_VERSION, run nothing, and every record is stale while stalePricing reports zero. The real fix publishes the constant out of the WASM guest. Related and now concrete: the Rust rate table and the TS model catalog are TWO sources for the same vendor facts, and only one of them has a schema that forces provenance.
